reason: @azure/msal-node 6.0.1 authorization-code parameter disclosure, present in word-addin only through the devDependency office-addin-debugging -> office-addin-dev-settings -> @microsoft/m365agentstoolkit-cli -> @azure/identity (`npm ls @azure/msal-node --omit=dev` is empty). That CLI signs a developer into Microsoft 365 for sideloading; the add-in has no MSAL code of its own and the production add-in image contains only the static bundle and server.mjs. The current upstream ranges require MSAL 6.x; this exception does not waive the advisory for any production dependency or other consumer. REMOVE WHEN: office-addin-debugging's declared range resolves @azure/msal-node >=7.1.0.

picomatch through 4.0.7 backtracks exponentially on single-branch repeated extglob PATTERNS such as +(*); the attacker must supply the glob. No release is patched. No source in backend/, frontend/, word-addin/ or packages/ imports picomatch, micromatch, fast-glob or tinyglobby, and every glob these tools compile comes from build, test or bundler configuration checked into this repository, never from a request or a document. Each scope names its exact dependents, so a new consumer of the package fails the gate. REMOVE WHEN: picomatch publishes a release outside the advisory's affected range and the lockfiles resolve it.

scopes.productionExposure: Reached only through @opennextjs/cloudflare -> @opennextjs/aws -> @node-minify/core -> @node-minify/utils -> fast-glob -> micromatch, the Cloudflare deploy build. The Docker image installs it with the rest of node_modules, but no request path loads it.

Reached in production only through @sentry/nextjs -> @rollup/plugin-commonjs and @rollup/pluginutils, which run while `next build` bundles the app; the other dependents (vite, vitest, fdir, tinyglobby, @ladle/react) are test and tooling packages. The Docker image installs it with the rest of node_modules, but no request path loads it.
